name: responsive_widths
description: Assert the chrome lays out cleanly across viewport widths. Until SetViewportSize existed the harness could not resize the app at all, so every other scenario ran at one fixed width and the entire responsive dimension of the UI was untested. Widths below ~800 logical are a KNOWN open defect (toolbar.watchlist_toggle clips) and are deliberately not asserted here — see docs/UI_AUDIT_2026-07-31.md.

steps.message: 1100 wide: clean. The pane-header right cluster collapses to icon-only when the labelled form would not fit its pane -- it is laid out from the right edge and does not wrap or scroll, so without that it ran over the tab strip and got cut (pane.overlay outside its clip). Collapse is per-PANE, not per-window: with two panes at 1280 each header is ~615px, so it collapses there too and that is correct. 900 wide still clips -- next threshold, not yet addressed.
Restored to 2400 and still clean — the resize is reversible, not one-way.

Re-maximized. MANDATORY: resizing un-maximizes the window, and every later scenario in this app instance would otherwise run at a size it was never written against. Deliberately NOT asserted: wait_frames counts FRAMES, not wall-clock, so it does not wait for the OS to finish the maximize -- asserting here caught a transient mid-resize clip on pane.overlay, which measurement showed sits well inside its clip rect once settled (right 1416 vs clip right 1669). The widths that matter are already asserted above; a racy check in a gate is worse than no check.
